title.narrative: Government and social partners develop and implement policies to manage migration, protect migrant workers and combat human trafficking in line with ILO principles

description.narrative: Many Lao workers, particularly women, migrate to Thailand and other countries, often through irregular channels due to costly and complicated official procedures. This increases exposure to exploitation, forced labour, and trafficking, with limited access to safe migration information, complaints mechanisms, and protection services. The ILO supports the Government of Lao PDR and social partners in developing and implementing fair and effective labour migration policies to protect migrant workers and prevent trafficking in persons in accordance with ILO principles. The intervention strengthens national legal and policy frameworks on labour migration, ensuring coherence with employment, skills, and social protection policies, and improving alignment with international labour standards. ILO provides technical assistance for establishing the Lao Employment Service Association to promote fair recruitment practices, enhance pre-departure training, especially for high-risk sectors such as fishing and seafood processing, and disseminate migration regulations to provincial authorities and stakeholders. Capacity-building efforts focus on recruitment agencies, Migrant Worker Resource Centres (MRCs), labour authorities, trade unions, civil society organizations, and cross-border service providers, aiming to improve coordination, case management, and service delivery to migrant workers. Awareness-raising campaigns in communities, schools, and workplaces inform workers of their rights and safe migration pathways. By increasing access to information, services, and safe recruitment channels, the intervention seeks to strengthen protection for migrant workers, especially for women, reduce irregular migration, and enhance national capacity to prevent labour exploitation and trafficking in persons.
